Find functions/methods by name and return complete bodies, imports and call sites.

file/folder to distinguish same-named symbols; receivers are included for Go.

methods, and JS/TS variables assigned arrow functions or function expressions.

Calls are syntactic expressions inside each definition, including nested
closures. They are NOT resolved targets or a guaranteed execution sequence.
Follow package aliases using the returned imports; use code_graph for indexed
callees and verify uncertain edges. Calls may include type conversions.

results do not prove absence (other declaration forms/languages may need ast_grep).
No build, code execution, LLM, graph generation, or dependencies are required.

summary: Match syntax patterns with ast-grep.
usage:
Search source structure with ast-grep and return complete matched code and line ranges.

Use for whole functions, methods, classes, and structural patterns. Use
search_files for literal text and code_graph for callers/callees. This tool
parses syntax, not semantic type resolution; verify receiver/package matches.
Choose a source file or narrow folder from the configured code projects.
Git ignores apply to directory searches; symlinks are not followed.

Supply exactly one native pattern or a native rule object encoded as JSON.
$NAME matches one syntax node; $$$NAME matches a sequence. Patterns depend on
language and declaration shape; a method pattern need not match a free function.

Go method body: language="Go",
pattern="func ($RECEIVER) SetPersonalLimits($$$ARGS) { $$$BODY }".
Go functions or methods by name, regardless of signature: language="Go",
rule='{"any":[{"kind":"function_declaration"},{"kind":"method_declaration"}],
"has":{"field":"name","regex":"^SetPersonalLimits$"}}'.
Python function: language="Python", pattern="def process($$$ARGS): $$$BODY".

Results contain the complete matched node once, including its signature/body
when a whole declaration is matched; adjacent doc comments are not included.
Use read_file for surrounding comments/imports or other source ranges. If
truncated, narrow the folder/pattern or request more matches. Empty results
do not prove a symbol is absent: check language, pattern shape, and ignores.

query.title: Query

summary: Search symbols and follow callers and callees. Offered when a selected code project has a generated graph.
usage:
Search and explore indexed source with CodeGraph's own SDK functions.

Start with search; it returns every exact-name overload, or text-search hits
when there is no exact name. Use code for a complete function body, context
for imports/types/references, and callees/callers for direct relationships.
Traverse follows all reachable outgoing calls; results are paginated, with
edges grouped by their source node on each page. Continue with next_offset.
Routes lists the indexed API registrations. Unresolved can be scoped to a node.

Nodes and edges retain native CodeGraph fields (filePath, startLine, metadata).
File paths are relative to path_base. Code is read with getCode only after its
file hash matches the index. Changed/missing source is reported, not silently
paired with stale symbol ranges. No code is shortened. Edge confidence and
resolvedBy are evidence, not guarantees: verify import/receiver resolution,
branches, middleware, SQL and side effects. A missing edge proves no absence.
These operations do not use an LLM, re-index, or modify the saved graph/source.

Use code_graph first: search for symbols, code for full bodies, context for imports/types, and traverse for
reachable calls. It uses the CodeGraph SDK directly; follow pagination and inspect edge metadata and unresolved
references. Then verify business rules, state changes, SQL and external effects with source-file tools. Graph paths
are relative to CODE_ROOT, as returned by the tool. Static edges are evidence, not proof of runtime execution.

summary: Draft an environment, servers, services, deployments, connections and relations in one call, by name.
usage:
Draft a whole picture in one call: an environment, its servers, the services and where they are deployed, the connections between them and their relations. Entries refer to each other by name, not id. Every part is optional.

Every write is a draft: it is added to the inventory as a draft that a person confirms or discards in the environment workspace. You may add drafts and change or remove drafts (yours or another agent's); a confirmed entry is changed only by people, so the tool refuses it: add a new draft instead, or describe the change in your answer. Read first (get_environment_model, list_servers, get_resource): every entry carries its status (draft or confirmed), so you do not add what is already there.

How names resolve: a name refers to an entry in this call first, then to a recorded entry (confirmed or draft) in this run or drafted by this session. A recorded confirmed entry named here is used as it is, never changed (its fields here are ignored, but its part_of still adds draft relations); a recorded draft is updated with the fields given; anything else is created as a draft (a new entry needs an environment, server or service in this run). environment names an existing environment or drafts a new one; every server listed and every server a deployment runs on joins it (a draft membership), and deployments and connections are in it.
- servers: name, hostname (An IP address or hostname without scheme, port, path or credentials (10.0.0.5, db-1.internal).), description, tags.
- services: name, service_type: unclassified (default), custom (your own code), builtin (an off-the-shelf product such as PostgreSQL, nginx or ClickHouse) or external (outside your servers, reached at an address: a SaaS API, object storage); service_role: unclassified (default), application, proxy, web_server, database, cache, message_broker, worker or other; description, owner, address (an external service), part_of (names of the services it is a component of).
- deployments: service and server (names), runtime (Free text: how it runs, such as systemd, docker, docker compose or k8s.), runtime_name (unit, container or pod name), port (1–65535), version, log_location. A deployment is the recorded one of that service on that server in the environment: with runtime_name the one with that runtime name, without it the only one there (when there are several, give runtime_name); else it is created.
- connections: from (a service name), to (a service name: an external service, or a service deployed in the environment) or to_host (An IP address or hostname without scheme, port, path or credentials (10.0.0.5, db-1.internal).), port (1–65535; needed for a host), protocol (Lowercase letters, digits or . + - (1–20), such as tcp (default), http, https, postgres or smtp.), description. A connection starts and ends at that service's deployment in the environment: from_server and to_server name the server only when the service runs on more than one, from_runtime_name and to_runtime_name the runtime name only when it runs more than once on that server.
- relations: from (a service name), kind: depends_on (needs another service to work), part_of (a component of another service) or built_from (built from a code project); to (a service name, or a code project name for built_from), description.
All or nothing: on any error nothing is written and the reply names the entry and the reason, such as "connections[0]: no service named clickhous. Known services: clickhouse, clickhouse-backup." The reply lists what was created, updated and used, each with kind, name and id.

Example: {
  "environment": "prod",
  "servers": [{"name": "app-1", "hostname": "10.0.0.5", "description": "Docker host"}],
  "services": [
    {"name": "clickhouse", "service_type": "builtin", "service_role": "database", "description": "Analytics store"},
    {"name": "clickhouse-backup", "service_type": "builtin", "service_role": "worker", "part_of": ["clickhouse"]},
    {"name": "backblaze-b2", "service_type": "external", "address": "s3.us-east-005.backblazeb2.com"}
  ],
  "deployments": [
    {"service": "clickhouse", "server": "app-1", "runtime": "docker compose", "runtime_name": "clickhouse",
     "port": 9000, "version": "clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.8"},
    {"service": "clickhouse-backup", "server": "app-1", "runtime": "docker compose",
     "runtime_name": "clickhouse-backup", "version": "altinity/clickhouse-backup:2.7.4"}
  ],
  "connections": [
    {"from": "clickhouse-backup", "from_server": "app-1", "to": "clickhouse", "to_server": "app-1",
     "port": 9000, "protocol": "tcp"},
    {"from": "clickhouse-backup", "to": "backblaze-b2", "port": 443, "protocol": "https"},
    {"from": "clickhouse", "to_host": "smtp.example.com", "port": 25, "protocol": "smtp"}
  ],
  "relations": [{"from": "clickhouse-backup", "kind": "depends_on", "to": "clickhouse"}]
}
